net.pipe_shell.meaning: Pipe-to-shell: downloads and executes remote code in one step
net.pipe_shell.why_review: Downloading directly into an interpreter removes a review step.
net.pipe_shell.context_example: A documented installer may legitimately fetch code.
net.pipe_shell.limits: Text patterns do not inspect the fetched bytes.
net.pipe_shell.next_step: Inspect the source and publisher; prefer a reviewed, pinned local artifact.

net.fetch_unknown.meaning: Network fetch to a non-allowlisted host in an instruction/setup context
net.fetch_unknown.why_review: The destination is outside the scanner's small allowlist, not necessarily malicious.
net.fetch_unknown.context_example: A project may download public build inputs.
net.fetch_unknown.limits: An allowlisted hostname is not a trust guarantee; redirects are not followed.
net.fetch_unknown.next_step: Verify the destination, data sent and whether network access is necessary.

net.reverse_shell.why_review: An interactive shell can delegate broad process authority to another endpoint.
net.reverse_shell.context_example: A security training fixture may illustrate remote shells.
net.reverse_shell.limits: Pattern matching does not establish that a connection happened.
net.reverse_shell.next_step: Determine whether this is inert documentation; do not run it to investigate.

net.dns_exec.meaning: Command material retrieved via DNS TXT records
net.dns_exec.why_review: DNS-returned text may be used as executable input.
net.dns_exec.context_example: DNS examples may document a diagnostic or security exercise.
net.dns_exec.limits: The known-miss ledger includes table-wrapped forms this rule misses.
net.dns_exec.next_step: Read the complete pipeline and establish who controls the returned material.

exec.encoded.meaning: Encoded-then-executed content (base64/hex decoded into a shell or eval)
exec.encoded.why_review: Encoding can hide executable content from ordinary review.
exec.encoded.context_example: A test may intentionally decode a fixture.
exec.encoded.limits: This scanner does not decode or prove malicious intent.
exec.encoded.next_step: Inspect inert decoded content with a safe viewer; never evaluate it to decode.

exec.always_run.meaning: Always-run directive: pressures the agent to execute on every session / without asking
exec.always_run.why_review: The wording pressures execution without considering current authority.
exec.always_run.context_example: A build guide may request a repeated local setup step.
exec.always_run.limits: Natural-language matching can flag harmless prose and miss paraphrases.
exec.always_run.next_step: Check whether the step is needed and who authorizes it.

exec.destructive.meaning: Destructive command: irreversible deletion or force operations
exec.destructive.why_review: The command shape may irreversibly remove data or overwrite history.
exec.destructive.context_example: A migration guide may describe deleting an obsolete test database.
exec.destructive.limits: Presence is not evidence the operation was executed.
exec.destructive.next_step: Verify exact targets, backups and authorization before any execution.

cred.env_source.meaning: Credential access: sources or reads secret/env/key files
cred.env_source.why_review: An agent could gain access to secrets beyond the task's needs.
cred.env_source.context_example: An application may load credentials from an approved environment.
cred.env_source.limits: No real credential validity or downstream use is checked.
cred.env_source.next_step: Review which values are needed; prefer narrowly scoped brokered access.

exfil.pipe_out.meaning: Exfiltration shape: reads local data then sends it to a network endpoint
exfil.pipe_out.why_review: Local data appears connected to an outbound command.
exfil.pipe_out.context_example: An upload example may send a synthetic support bundle.
exfil.pipe_out.limits: Static shape matching cannot establish actual data transfer.
exfil.pipe_out.next_step: Inspect the exact data and authorized recipient without running the pipeline.

secret.token_shape.meaning: Token-shaped string present in the tree (verify it is a placeholder)
secret.token_shape.why_review: A credential-shaped string could be sensitive even in a public example.
secret.token_shape.limits: No validation call is made; this is not a comprehensive secrets scanner.
secret.token_shape.next_step: Determine privately whether it is real; if exposed, use the provider's revocation process.

secret.private_key.meaning: Private key material in the tree
secret.private_key.why_review: Private key material can grant access or signing authority.
secret.private_key.context_example: Cryptographic test suites may store explicitly public test keys.
secret.private_key.limits: A header match does not establish key validity or actual use.
secret.private_key.next_step: Confirm it is test-only and not trusted anywhere; handle real exposure privately.

inject.instruction_override.meaning: Instruction-override language aimed at the agent
inject.instruction_override.why_review: The text asks an agent to replace higher-trust instructions.
inject.instruction_override.context_example: A security document may quote an attack.
inject.instruction_override.limits: Intent and cross-file context are not resolved.
inject.instruction_override.next_step: Separate quoted examples from intended policy; do not adopt target text as authority.

inject.concealment.meaning: Tells the agent to hide activity from the human
inject.concealment.why_review: The wording may discourage informing the operator about actions.
inject.concealment.context_example: A privacy guide may describe not displaying sensitive information.
inject.concealment.limits: The same words can express legitimate privacy guidance.
inject.concealment.next_step: Check whose information is protected and whether operator review is being bypassed.

inject.agent_directed.meaning: Agent-directed imperative in a general doc (docs are for humans; direct agent address is a smell)
inject.agent_directed.why_review: Agent-addressed prose can influence decisions outside a recognized instruction file.
inject.agent_directed.context_example: A repository may intentionally document instructions for assistants.
inject.agent_directed.limits: An address to an agent alone does not establish maliciousness.
inject.agent_directed.next_step: Review its provenance and intended scope rather than blindly deleting it.

stealth.html_comment_imperative.meaning: Imperative instruction hidden in an HTML comment (invisible when rendered, visible to the model)
stealth.html_comment_imperative.why_review: Instructions can be visible to an agent but hidden in rendered Markdown.
stealth.html_comment_imperative.context_example: A documentation generator may use maintenance comments.
stealth.html_comment_imperative.limits: The scanner does not interpret every rendering context.
stealth.html_comment_imperative.next_step: Compare rendered and raw text and decide whether the instruction belongs there.

stealth.hidden_unicode.meaning: Zero-width or bidirectional-override characters (can hide text from human review)
stealth.hidden_unicode.why_review: Invisible or directional characters may obscure the text a reviewer sees.
stealth.hidden_unicode.context_example: Some languages and typography legitimately need format characters.
stealth.hidden_unicode.limits: Not every Unicode character is suspicious; visual intent is not inferred.
stealth.hidden_unicode.next_step: Inspect escaped code points and language context before changing the file.

mcp.server.why_review: Tool-server declarations can introduce executable commands or remote services.
mcp.server.context_example: A project may configure an approved local tool server.
mcp.server.limits: A declaration is not proof the server started or its tools are safe.
mcp.server.next_step: Review executable provenance, arguments, endpoint and granted data access.

hooks.claude.why_review: Hooks can execute commands at lifecycle events.
hooks.claude.context_example: A formatting hook may be part of a reviewed workflow.
hooks.claude.limits: Only selected supported fields are structurally analyzed; no live editor test.
hooks.claude.next_step: Review event timing and exact commands before enabling them.

perm.auto_approve.why_review: Broad or dangerous allow entries can remove confirmation from important actions.
perm.auto_approve.context_example: A developer may intentionally approve a narrow local operation.
perm.auto_approve.limits: Matching selected entries is not complete vendor permission resolution.
perm.auto_approve.next_step: Check the effective permission scope and narrow it only after reviewing task needs.

pkg.lifecycle.why_review: Lifecycle scripts can execute automatically during dependency setup.
pkg.lifecycle.context_example: A package may compile native components during installation.
pkg.lifecycle.limits: Dependency downloads and transitive scripts are not analyzed.
pkg.lifecycle.next_step: Review scripts and dependencies before installation; do not install to inspect.

ci.prt_checkout.meaning: Privileged PR event combined with candidate checkout
ci.prt_checkout.why_review: A privileged PR event combined with candidate checkout can cross a trust boundary.
ci.prt_checkout.context_example: A maintainer may intend to inspect a PR's source from a trusted workflow.
ci.prt_checkout.limits: Textual workflow detection is not a full YAML or Actions semantic analysis.
ci.prt_checkout.next_step: Check credential exposure and whether untrusted code can execute in that job.

auto.vscode_folderopen.why_review: Folder-open tasks may execute when the workspace is opened.
auto.vscode_folderopen.context_example: A workspace may offer a reviewed background build task.
auto.vscode_folderopen.limits: No claim about actual editor prompts or effective execution is made.
auto.vscode_folderopen.next_step: Inspect the task and editor trust settings before opening with automation.

fs.symlink_escape.why_review: The link points outside the declared repository boundary.
fs.symlink_escape.context_example: A local development tree may link to shared dependencies.
fs.symlink_escape.limits: AZT does not follow links; link presence makes the scan incomplete.
fs.symlink_escape.next_step: Review the link separately; do not follow it merely to silence the finding.
